feed.title: Vision Field Notes
feed.subtitle: Practical computer vision and edge AI, from someone who runs it in production.

entry.title: Site Surveys: What to Check Before Promising a Result
entry.summary: A short visit or remote survey before quoting catches most problems that sink camera analytics projects. What to check, record and ask.

entry.title: Reading YOLO Training Curves: When to Stop and What to Change
entry.summary: What YOLO loss and metric curves tell you, the shapes of overfitting and under-training, and the quirks in the curves that are not problems.

entry.title: CPU-Only Inference: Getting the Most from OpenVINO and ONNX Runtime
entry.summary: No GPU on site? Detectors can still run on x86 CPUs. How to export, tune threads, pick input size and precision, and measure what a CPU can carry.

entry.title: Managing Per-Camera Configuration at Scale
entry.summary: Zones, thresholds, schedules and streams for hundreds of cameras: how to layer defaults and overrides, validate them and keep them versioned.

entry.title: Main Stream or Substream: Choosing Resolution and Bitrate for Analytics
entry.summary: IP cameras offer a full-quality main stream and a lighter substream. Which to analyse depends on object size, model input and decode budget.

entry.title: Turning Down a Computer Vision Project (and Offering Something Better)
entry.summary: Some vision projects should not be accepted as asked. How to spot them, say no without losing the client, and offer a version that works.

entry.title: Single-Class or Multi-Class: When to Merge or Split Detection Classes
entry.summary: Should car, van and truck be one class or three? How to decide a detector's classes, and why labelling fine and training coarse keeps options open.

entry.title: Watchdogs and Self-Recovery for Unattended Edge Boxes
entry.summary: An edge box nobody can reach must recover on its own. Hardware watchdogs, systemd restarts, application health checks and remote alerts, layered.

entry.title: Deduplicating Video Frames Before Labelling
entry.summary: Most frames from a fixed camera are near-copies. How to pick frames worth labelling with difference checks, hashes and embeddings, keeping rare cases.

entry.title: Profiling a Python Vision Pipeline: Finding the Real Bottleneck
entry.summary: Before optimising the model, find where the time actually goes. Stage timers, sampling profilers and the usual hidden costs in Python video pipelines.

entry.title: How Many Frames per Second Does Your Analytics Need?
entry.summary: Analysing every frame is rarely necessary. How to pick an analysis frame rate from object speed, view size, filters and trackers, and test it.

entry.title: Why a Detector's Confidence Is Not a Probability
entry.summary: A box scored 0.8 is not right 80% of the time. What confidence scores are, why they shift between models and classes, and what that means for thresholds.

entry.title: Estimating a Computer Vision Project: Where the Time Really Goes
entry.summary: Model training is rarely the long part. How to estimate a vision project honestly: data access, labelling, integration, site testing and waiting.

entry.title: Updating Models on Edge Devices Without Bricking Them
entry.summary: Pushing a new model to boxes you cannot reach is risky. Atomic switches, self-tests, staged rollouts and automatic rollback make updates safe and boring.

entry.title: Pseudo-Labelling with a Larger Model: Time Saver or Data Poison?
entry.summary: Using a big model to pre-label images can cut annotation time, or quietly copy its mistakes into your dataset. How to use pseudo-labels safely.

entry.title: Building a Replay Set of Recorded Footage
entry.summary: A small, curated library of recorded clips with known events lets you test every pipeline change against reality. What to include and how to keep it.

entry.title: Alerts at the Wrong Time of Day: Time Zones, DST and Camera Clocks
entry.summary: Alerts that fire correctly but at the wrong time usually come from clocks: drifting cameras, servers in UTC, daylight saving. How to handle time properly.

entry.title: Writing a Results Report a Non-Technical Client Will Read
entry.summary: How to report computer vision results to people who will never read a mAP table: lead with the answer, use their units, show examples and state limits.

entry.title: Preprocessing Mismatches That Silently Cost Accuracy
entry.summary: A model only works on inputs prepared the way it was trained. Resize method, colour order, normalisation and padding mismatches, and how to catch them.

entry.title: Measuring Label Quality with Annotator Agreement
entry.summary: Double-label a sample, match the boxes and count disagreements. How to measure label quality, what it means for small objects, and what to do next.

entry.title: Hardware Video Decoding: Why Decode Is Often the Real Bottleneck
entry.summary: Every stream is decoded at full resolution before the model sees it. Why decoding can cost more than inference, and how to use hardware decoders.

entry.title: The EU AI Act Delay: What Camera Analytics Teams Should Know
entry.summary: The Digital Omnibus moved the EU AI Act's high-risk deadlines to December 2027. What changed, what did not, and what it means for video analytics.

entry.title: Metrics and Logging for a Vision Service
entry.summary: Which numbers to collect from a live video analytics service, per camera and per stage, so you see problems before the client does, and how to log.

entry.title: Day/Night Switching: Why Detections Change When the IR Filter Flips
entry.summary: When a camera switches to infrared night mode, the image changes completely. What that does to the model, why cameras flap at dusk, and what to do.

entry.title: Writing an Annotation Guide Labellers Can Follow
entry.summary: Labels are only as consistent as the rules behind them. What to put in an annotation guide, how to show edge cases and how to keep it current.

entry.title: Microchip Completes Its Hailo Acquisition: What It Means for Edge Vision Projects
entry.summary: Microchip closed its acquisition of edge AI chipmaker Hailo in September 2026. What is known, what is not, and how to manage accelerator vendor risk.

entry.title: Handover Documentation for a Computer Vision System
entry.summary: What to hand over when a vision project ends so the client can run, monitor, retrain and fix it without you: the documents, files and records that matter.

entry.title: YOLO27 Announced: What to Check Before You Switch
entry.summary: Ultralytics announced YOLO27 in September 2026. What was actually said, what is still unknown, and how to evaluate it on your own data when it ships.

entry.title: Versioning Datasets and Models Together
entry.summary: When a deployed model misbehaves, you need to know exactly which data, labels, code and settings made it. A light system for tracing every model back.

entry.title: Input Resolution or Model Size: Which to Increase for Small Objects
entry.summary: When a detector misses small objects, a bigger model and a bigger input both cost compute. Why input size usually helps more, and when it does not.
